neighbours.label: a whole nation's population or 'the public' as the subject whose opinion or mood is being reported (Americans are..., the British people want...), as against a specific group, committee or profession in the same frame
fire: A new poll suggests that Britons are losing patience with the rail strikes.
Analysts say the French people want the pension reform scrapped entirely.
Ministers fear the public will not accept another rise in fuel duty.
Most Australians are now opposed to the new mining tax, the survey found.
Commentators believe Germans are weary of the long coalition talks.
The senator insisted that the American people deserve a straight answer.
Pollsters found that Mexicans are deeply divided over the judicial reform.
Officials admit the public has grown suspicious of the vaccine rollout.
quiet: A new memo suggests that nurses are losing patience with the night shifts.
Analysts say the board members want the merger plan scrapped entirely.
Ministers fear the union will not accept another freeze in wages.
Most shareholders are now opposed to the new bonus scheme, the report found.
Commentators believe the players are weary of the long training camp.
The coach insisted that the team deserves a straight answer from the owners.
Organisers found that the volunteers are deeply divided over the new rota.
Officials admit the jury has grown suspicious of the main witness.

predictions: fire 0.3-0.6 on or just after the populace noun (Britons, the French people, the public); specific groups (nurses, the board, the jury) in identical frames below 0.1
